description:
COACTUPC's date-edit engine on its INVALID paths - the counterpart to case09, which owns the clean traversal. This case owns the REJECTION arms and the guard-chain ordering that makes each of them reachable (gate G30). PROVENANCE (practice B12, AAP 0.7.6 risk R-A): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cpy/CSUTLDPY.cpy, app/cpy/CSUTLDWY.cpy, app/cpy/CSSETATY.cpy and app/cbl/COACTUPC.cbl together with app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY and the decoded fixture rows, and was NOT captured from a live COBOL execution - running the 28 legacy programs is impossible in this environment against eight independently verified blockers. No user-specified Rule governs this file: review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided", so enterprise best practice B1-B12 governs instead; no rule has been invented and the bar is not lowered. FOUR SITES, FOUR DIFFERENT SHAPES OF FAILURE. COACTUPC performs EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD THRU EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-EXIT four times in one turn - Open Date [L1478-L1482], Expiry Date [L1490-L1494], Reissue Date [L1503-L1507] and Date of Birth [L1533-L1538] - so a single turn can drive four different rejection arms, and each one here is a different KIND of rejection. (1) OPEN DATE 2101/11/20 drives the CENTURY arm [CSUTLDPY:L70-L84]. CSUTLDWY declares only 88 THIS-CENTURY VALUE 20 [L9] and 88 LAST-CENTURY VALUE 19 [L10], and L70-L71 accepts a year ONLY IF THIS-CENTURY OR LAST-CENTURY, so 2101 is rejected exactly as 1899 would be. The copybook says so out loud at [L66-L68] - being unable to imagine COBOL in the 2100s, it codes only 19 and 20 as valid - and practice B5 forbids widening it. Tail ' : Century is not valid.' [L79]. Flags left behind: WS-EDIT-OPEN-YEAR-FLG '0' (FLG-OPEN-YEAR-NOT-OK), WS-EDIT-OPEN-MONTH LOW-VALUES (FLG-OPEN-MONTH-ISVALID), WS-EDIT-OPEN-DAY LOW-VALUES (FLG-OPEN-DAY-ISVALID) - month 11 and day 20 both pass their own paragraphs, because a failed year does NOT stop them: EDIT-YEAR-CCYY's GO TO EDIT-YEAR-CCYY-EXIT [L42, L58, L83] leaves only ITS paragraph and the performed range falls straight on into EDIT-MONTH [L91] and EDIT-DAY [L150]. (2) EXPIRY DATE 2025/04/31 drives the MULTI-FLAG cross-component arm [L213-L226]: IF NOT WS-31-DAY-MONTH AND WS-DAY-31, which sets BOTH FLG-DAY-NOT-OK [L216] AND FLG-MONTH-NOT-OK [L217]. April is absent from 88 WS-31-DAY-MONTH VALUES 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12 [CSUTLDWY:L21-L23] and 31 satisfies 88 WS-DAY-31 [L30]. Note what must be true for this arm to be REACHED at all: day 31 has to PASS EDIT-DAY first, and it does, because 88 WS-VALID-DAY VALUES 1 THROUGH 31 [L28-L29] admits 31. A month/day contradiction is only detectable once both components are individually legal, which is exactly why EDIT-DAY-MONTH-YEAR exists as a fourth paragraph rather than being folded into EDIT-DAY. Flags left behind: EXPIRY-YEAR LOW-VALUES, EXPIRY-MONTH '0', EXPIRY-DAY '0'. (3) REISSUE DATE 202A/05/20 drives the NOT-NUMERIC arm [L48-L61], whose tail is ' must be 4 digit number.' [L54] - WITH NO ' : ' PREFIX, unlike every sibling literal in the copybook. That inconsistency is reproduced byte for byte and NOT normalised (practice B5). Flags left behind: REISSUE-YEAR '0', REISSUE-MONTH LOW-VALUES, REISSUE-DAY LOW-VALUES. (4) DATE OF BIRTH 1961/06/blank drives the DAY-BLANK arm [L154-L165], which sets FLG-DAY-BLANK 'B' [L157] and not '0'. It is the only one of the four whose flag is 'B', and that distinction is observable - see THE '*' OVERLAY below. Because WS-EDIT-DT-OF-BIRTH-ISVALID is consequently false, [L1539-L1543] does NOT perform EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH, so the ':cannot be in the future ' arm [L363] is not reached here and is not asserted. THE ARM ORDER IS THE BEHAVIOUR (gate G30). EDIT-YEAR-CCYY opens PESSIMISTICALLY with SET FLG-YEAR-NOT-OK [L27] and then tests blank-or-LOW-VALUES [L30], then IS NOT NUMERIC [L48], then century [L70], each with GO TO EDIT-YEAR-CCYY-EXIT on failure, reaching SET FLG-YEAR-ISVALID [L86] only if all three pass. EDIT-MONTH repeats the shape [L92 through L143] with its own inversion - the range test at [L111] precedes the numeric test at [L126], the opposite of EDIT-DAY - and EDIT-DAY inverts the opening instead, setting FLG-DAY-ISVALID FIRST [L152]. All three asymmetries are preserved as written. THE FIRST FAILING GUARD WINS AND THE LATER ONES NEVER RUN: 2101 is tested for blankness and numeric class before the century test that rejects it, while 202A never reaches the century test at all - so no case can assert the century message for a non-numeric year, and this one does not. NO CSUTLDTC CALL - THE COMPLEMENT OF case09, AND THIS CASE'S SHARPEST ASSERTION. 88 WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-VALID VALUE LOW-VALUES [CSUTLDWY:L44] is declared on the THREE-BYTE GROUP WS-EDIT-DATE-FLGS [L43], so it holds only when the year, month and day bytes are ALL LOW-VALUES. The gate at [CSUTLDPY:L274-L278] reads IF WS-EDIT-DATE-IS-VALID CONTINUE ELSE GO TO EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-EXIT, and that GO TO jumps clean over EDIT-DATE-LE [L284-L321] and therefore over the CALL 'CSUTLDTC' at [L293-L296]. Every one of the four dates here leaves at least one flag byte at '0' or 'B', so all four leave the range early - the Expiry date at [L225] from inside EDIT-DAY-MONTH-YEAR itself, the other three at [L277] - and CSUTLDTC is called ZERO times. expectedMessages therefore carries NO WS_MESSAGE_80 entry at all, where case09 carries four; that absence is the assertion, not an omission, and it is the one statement about the L274 gate that a valid-path case cannot make. FIRST-MESSAGE-WINS, SO EXACTLY ONE TEXT SURVIVES. Every message site is wrapped in IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF, and WS-RETURN-MSG is PIC X(75) with 88 WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF VALUE SPACES [COACTUPC:L479-L480], reset once per turn at [L876]. Only the EARLIEST failing edit's text sticks. Account Status is edited first [L1472-L1476] and 'Y' passes 1220-EDIT-YESNO [L1856] silently, so the Open Date century message claims the slot, and the other three date arms - along with the later FICO, state/zip and phone-2 failures - each compose their text under a guard that is already false. That is why the three suppressed arms are asserted through their FLAGS and their ATTRIBUTES instead of through their text. The sibling that owns each literal as a surviving message is named so no arm looks unclaimed: case13 owns the 26-character 'Current Cycle Credit Limit' truncated to the X(25) width of WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME [L53], case14 owns 'Account Status must be Y or N.', case11 owns the phone-2 area-code text and case02 owns 'No input received'. THE COMPOSED MESSAGE, SPAN BY SPAN. STRING FUNCTION TRIM(WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME) ' : Century is not valid.' DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-RETURN-MSG [L76-L82]. 'Open Date' is 9 characters and fits WS-EDIT-VARIABLE-NAME PIC X(25) whole, so FUNCTION TRIM returns it entire - as it does for 'Expiry Date' (11), 'Reissue Date' (12) and 'Date of Birth' (13). None of the four date labels is truncated, which is precisely what distinguishes them from case13's 26-character label. 9 + 24 = 33 characters are transferred. COBOL STRING does not space-fill the remainder of its receiver, but WS-RETURN-MSG was SPACES on entry, so the residue is spaces and the 75-byte image is those 33 characters followed by 42 spaces. MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO ERRMSGO [L2981] then widens 75 to the ERRMSGO PIC X(78) that app/cpy-bms/COACTUP.CPY declares, adding three more spaces. Both widths are asserted - the 75-byte image on DISPLAY_LINE and the 78-byte image on SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 - which is ONE message observed at its two declared widths rather than two messages (practices B8 and B11). THE '*' OVERLAY, AND WHY EXACTLY ONE FIELD CARRIES IT (gate G38). CSSETATY reads IF (FLG-x-NOT-OK OR FLG-x-BLANK) AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER MOVE DFHRED TO xC, and then IF FLG-x-BLANK MOVE '*' TO xO. COACTUPC wires it per date COMPONENT rather than per date: OPEN-YEAR/MONTH/DAY at [L3214, L3220, L3226], EXPIRY-* at [L3238, L3244, L3250], REISSUE-* at [L3262, L3268, L3274] and DT-OF-BIRTH-* at [L3316, L3322, L3328]. Five components fail, so five carry DFHRED - OPNYEARC, EXPMONC, EXPDAYC, RISYEARC and DOBDAYC - and the other seven date components stay DFHDFCOL, which is the positive statement that they passed. Only DOBDAYC's flag is 'B', so DOBDAYO alone takes the '*': 3203-SHOW-UPDATED-VALUES [L2870] first moves ACUP-NEW-CUST-DOB-DAY - LOW-VALUES, because 1100-RECEIVE-MAP maps a blank component to LOW-VALUES [L1270-L1275] - into DOBDAYO [L2929], and 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS [L2986] then overwrites it with '*' space-filled to the X(2) the map declares, giving '* '. 3200 runs before 3300 inside 3000-SEND-MAP [L2649-L2661], so the overlay lands last and is what the screen carries. Colour and highlight are ATTRIBUTE METADATA and never payload members; the '*' is different in kind, because the COBOL moves it into the payload item itself. REACHING THE EDITS AT ALL. This is the post-fetch turn: CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, without which neither the DFHRED nor the '*' would be applied at all), and the inbound ACUP area carries change action 'S' (ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS), so [L1433] is false and the search-key-only shortcut [L1435-L1446] is not taken. WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA carries the full 873-byte ACUP area - the action byte followed by the ACUP-OLD account and customer image - and 160 + 873 = 1033 = EIBCALEN exactly, so the commarea arithmetic checks itself. Carrying ACUP-OLD in the PAYLOAD rather than in server state is what gate G37 requires, and it is what makes the next gate genuine: 1205-COMPARE-OLD-NEW [L1460, L1681-L1705] is a single conjunction, and ACUP-NEW-OPEN-DATE '21011120' differs from ACUP-OLD-OPEN-DATE '20141120', so it sets CHANGE-HAS-OCCURRED [L1703] and GO TOes its own exit - never reaching SET NO-CHANGES-DETECTED [L1769]. That matters more than it looks: NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is an 88 declared on WS-RETURN-MSG itself [L491], so had it fired it would have consumed the message slot before a single date was edited. The short-circuit at [L1463-L1468] is therefore not taken and SET ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK [L1470] runs. THE SEED IS REAL FIXTURE DATA AND ITS OWN FAILURES ARE PRESERVED. All four rows come from app/data/ASCII: acctdata row 0 and custdata row 0, cardxref row 48 seeded RAW at 36 bytes with the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared rather than left implicit (gate G16), and carddata row 48. The stored customer cannot pass COACTUPC's full edit suite - CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE is 274 where 1275-EDIT-FICO-SCORE [L2514] requires 300 to 850, and the state/zip cross-field check and the phone-2 area code fail behind it - so ACSTFCOC, ACSSTTEC, ACSZIPCC and ACSPH2AC are DFHRED here exactly as they are in case09. Those four are the seed's own baseline rather than this case's subject; fabricating clean values to hide them would break the rule that every payload byte traces to a fixture byte or a PICTURE clause (practices B11 and B12). The five date components are the only fields this case alters, and each alteration is a single operator keystroke away from the stored value: 2014 to 2101, 05 to 04, 20 to 31, 2025 to 202A, and 08 to blank. THE CURSOR IS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED. The cursor EVALUATE [L3009-L3167] is ordered by screen position and the first match wins. WHEN FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA [L3010] is FALSE, which is subtle: FOUND-ACCOUNT-DATA is an 88 on WS-INFO-MSG [L466-L467] rather than a state flag, and 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG [L2955] has already overwritten WS-INFO-MSG with PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES because 3250 precedes 3300 in 3000-SEND-MAP. WHEN NO-CHANGES-DETECTED [L3011] is FALSE for the same kind of reason - it is an 88 on WS-RETURN-MSG, which holds the century text. FLG-ACCTFILTER-* are false [L1454] and Account Status passed [L3017-L3019], so the first TRUE arm is WHEN FLG-OPEN-YEAR-NOT-OK [L3021] and the cursor lands on OPNYEARL - the EARLIEST failing component on the screen, not the last, and not case09's ACSTFCOL. INFOMSGO is PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES because 3250's EVALUATE takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK [L2964-L2965, literal at L470-L471]; INFOMSGH is DFHBMASB because WS-INFO-MSG is non-blank [L3567-L3570] and FKEY12H is DFHBMASB because ACUP-CHANGES-MADE holds while ACUP-CHANGES-OKAYED-AND-DONE does not [L3573-L3575], while FKEY05H stays at its default because PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is false. ERRMSGC stays DFHDFCOL because COACTUPC never assigns it - the only statement touching that field is MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO ERRMSGO [L2981]. AADDGRPO is ten LOW-VALUES rather than ten spaces because 1100-RECEIVE-MAP maps the blank group id to LOW-VALUES [L1213-L1215]. NOTHING IS WRITTEN AND THE RETURN CODE IS 0. expectedWrites is empty and all four datasets are asserted unchanged at their copybook widths 300/500/150/50 with FILLER included (gates G19 and G21), which is correct because this turn reaches no file verb at all: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION [L2562] takes WHEN ACUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK -> CONTINUE [L2596-L2597] and only its ACUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED / PFK12 arm reads. The transaction returns to itself pseudo-conversationally. COACTUPC sets no COBOL RETURN-CODE on any path, and CSUTLDTC's own MOVE WS-SEVERITY-N TO RETURN-CODE cannot contribute here for the simple reason that CSUTLDTC is never called. GATES: G15, G16, G18 (diff count zero), G30 (this case owns the date-engine arm ordering), G37, G38 (the DFHRED highlight and the '*' blank overlay apply only under CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), G51 (unit kind CONTROLLER_POJO: account.AccountUpdateController built through its own constructor with the real account.AccountDateValidator and util.DateUtilityJob injected - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no JobLauncher). NON-APPLICABLE, STATED EXPLICITLY: G32 does not apply because CBSTM03A is the only program with backward loop-forming GO TOs and this is not it; G35 does not apply because COACTUPC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and this path raises no AbendException.

OBSERVATION SCOPE, STATED SO IT CANNOT BE MISREAD AS AN OMISSION. COACTUPC contains no DISPLAY verb - no CICS program does - so this case declares no DISPLAY_LINE and no SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 message. WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) at :479 leaves the program through MOVE WS-RETURN-MSG TO ERRMSGO OF CACTUPAO at :2981 followed by EXEC CICS SEND MAP, and ERRMSGO is pinned byte for byte inside expectedResponse.sends at its declared PIC X(78) width. Declaring it a second time on a message channel would make one difference report as two and would invent an emission the program does not perform. The eighty-byte WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT of each CALL 'CSUTLDTC' (app/cpy/CSUTLDPY.cpy:293 into app/cpy/CSUTLDWY.cpy:60-85) IS declared, on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel and in call order, because nothing in the response exposes it and its count is itself an assertion about how far the edit chain ran.

THE CARRIED AREA, AND WHY IT IS DECLARED IN FULL. DFHCOMMAREA carries CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA together and :890-892 moves the second in whole, so the case declares all 873 bytes the copybook at :652-849 defines: ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION X(1), then ACUP-OLD-DETAILS and ACUP-NEW-DETAILS at 436 bytes each. The action is 'S' - 88 ACUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :659 - which is the state 3202-SHOW-ORIGINAL-VALUES leaves after a successful fetch and the only state in which 1100-RECEIVE-MAP does NOT return early at :1060-1062 and 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS therefore edits all forty-three writable items. ACUP-OLD-DETAILS is the snapshot 9500-STORE-FETCHED-DATA built from the seeded ACCTDAT and CUSTDAT rows, with the three account dates and the date of birth carried at PIC X(08) rather than the record's PIC X(10) because the group drops the separators. ACUP-NEW-DETAILS is declared at LOW-VALUES throughout, which is what INITIALIZE ACUP-NEW-DETAILS at :1047 leaves before the re-staging: whatever a warm turn arrived carrying is discarded there, so declaring anything else would describe a state the program overwrites before reading.

WHY THIS CASE EMITS NO EIGHTY-BYTE MESSAGE. All four date groups are rejected by the LOCAL edits in app/cpy/CSUTLDPY.cpy before EDIT-DATE-LE is reached, so CALL 'CSUTLDTC' at CSUTLDPY:293 never runs and no WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT is produced. Open date 2101-11-20: the century test rejects 21. Expiry date 2025-04-31: NOT WS-31-DAY-MONTH AND WS-DAY-31 rejects it with 'Cannot have 31 days in this month.' and jumps to EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD-EXIT. Reissue date 202A-05-20: the four-digit year test rejects a non-numeric year. Date of birth 1961-06 with a blank day: the day-must-be-supplied test rejects it. A count of zero is therefore an assertion in its own right - a translation that called the date utility anyway would emit four messages here.

fields.ERRMSGO: Open Date : Century is not valid.
